sources_considered.why: Repeated unselected generations directly test reliability on relations, negation, and counts.
Broader human evaluation across six image generators, including evidence of stronger performance on easier compositions.
Verified the cited version's June 19, 2024 availability.
Relevant additional benchmark, but the selected human evaluations provide sufficient evidence with fewer automated-grading assumptions.

evidence_items.explanation: The study uses repeated unselected generations and human judgments, finding substantial failures across relational, negative, and numerical constraints. It supports unreliable adherence on these tasks, without implying that every individual prompt is unreliable.

Across six image generators, the strongest system, DALL-E 3, averaged 3.4 out of 5 on advanced prompts, indicating several minor discrepancies. Its stronger 4.3 rating on basic prompts is material counterevidence to an unrestricted reading that language-image alignment was poor on every kind of request.

unresolved_gaps: The studies do not establish that internal representations are superficial.
The evidence does not justify a universal claim that no prompt or task offers reliable results.
